gaps.justification: Advanced communication skills needed for explaining automated systems and algorithmic logic to stakeholders not previously expected; role expands to technical advocacy and education.
gaps.name: Technical Communication of Automated Methods
gaps.description: Ability to clearly explain the technical aspects, risks, and operational improvements of automated and AI-enabled sampling and integration systems to a variety of stakeholders.

id: Acquire, Integrate & Process Data - Transition to Automation
update description: Data acquisition and integration activities must transition to orchestrated, automated pipelines, prioritizing administrative and alternative sources over survey-based collections. Stakeholder engagement is to focus on system-level integration, digital data acquisition, and process automation.
impact reasoning: The Specialist role shifts from managing largely manual or semi-automated data integration and acquisition projects to designing, implementing, and optimizing automated, orchestrated data pipelines. Responsibilities encompass not just acquiring data, but architecting digital workflows, specifying and negotiating API-based data exchange, and maintaining real-time pipelines. Stakeholder outreach prioritizes digital system connectivity, sustainable integration, and joint automation development over temporary or ad hoc data-transfer agreements.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - Bullet 1
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Manages activities must now encompass the design, implementation, and ongoing automation of digital data integration pipelines, including automated error handling, continuous ingestion, and dashboard-based oversight.

gaps.justification: Current description focuses on project or batch-based management; new requirements demand system architecture, automation, and digital process oversight skills.
gaps.name: Digital Acquisition Pipeline Design
gaps.description: Designing and maintaining automated, orchestrated pipelines for integrating alternative and administrative data sources at scale.

gaps.justification: Manual or semi-automated activities will be replaced by automated monitoring; thus, the ability to configure, optimize, and interpret real-time dashboards is required.
gaps.name: Dashboard-Centric Process Monitoring
gaps.description: Using, customizing, and interpreting real-time dashboards for monitoring automated data pipelines and paradata.

gaps.justification: Greater dependency on event-driven, API-based architectures for data flow and negotiation.
gaps.name: API Specifications & Integration
gaps.description: Understanding technical, security, and operational standards for negotiating and maintaining API-based data acquisition agreements.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - Bullet 2
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Outreach and collaboration now center on system-level integration and digital transformation with stakeholders, driving digital trust, shared API standards, and collaborative platform automation.

gaps.justification: Historical engagement emphasized relationships and user needs; automation requires familiarity with institutional digital integration practices and legal/data governance of system-level arrangements.
gaps.name: System-Level Data Integration Agreements
gaps.description: Knowledge of orchestrating formal digital data-sharing arrangements, including technical standardization, data privacy, security, and long-term interoperability.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - Bullet 3
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Project leadership will focus on the continuous optimization, monitoring, and governance of automated digital data streams. Mitigation strategies will shift to managing issues with digital flows, exception-handling mechanisms, and real-time system failures.

gaps.justification: Mitigation now means exception management within automated pipelines, needing new types of diagnostic and troubleshooting capability.
gaps.name: Automated Exception Management
gaps.description: Ability to detect, diagnose, and resolve automated process failures in digital data environments using monitoring tools and event logs.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - Bullet 5
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Negotiation activities will require fluency in technical (API/data platform) standards and security/privacy obligations in digital acquisition arrangements.

gaps.justification: Negotiations increasingly involve API standard, security, and legal-technical alignment rather than conventional data sharing agreements.
gaps.name: API/Data Platform Negotiation
gaps.description: Technical and legal negotiation skills for formalizing API-based, automated data sharing and integration arrangements.

update description: Transition from manual, bespoke integration processes and ad hoc linkages to automated, metadata-rich, modular data pipelines. Hands-on manipulation gives way to configuration and management of reusable integration components, event-driven processes, and standardized, platform-enabled workflows. Emphasis increases on pipeline logic, metadata management, interface governance, and auditability/provenance; skills shift toward FAIR principles, microservices, logic abstraction, and automated interoperability.
impact reasoning: The work-description's majority of integration and linkage responsibilities must update from manual operations—writing custom scripts, ad hoc data harmonization, and one-off integrations—to skills and responsibilities central to automated, reusable, and metadata-driven platforms. The focus of the role becomes designing and configuring these pipelines, monitoring exceptions, and evolving rules, as opposed to writing code for each new project. Stakeholder collaboration and analytical authorship will increasingly require understanding of the interoperability and re-use principles that underpin these pipeline systems.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities: 'Manages activities related to: data integration, data manipulation, data analytics, processing...'; 'Leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources...'; 'Implementation of various tools or software...'; 'Ensuring overall quality and completeness of program results.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: These activities move away from project-by-project integration and spreadsheet/database manipulation toward specification, governance, monitoring, and continuous improvement of standardized pipeline components and automation processes. The Specialist’s tasks involve configuring, maintaining, and evolving data integration platforms/as-a-service, shifting direct effort from custom coding to logic definition, exception handling, and meta-data curation.

gaps.justification: As manual integration processes are replaced by automated platforms and reusable modules, proficiency in developing, configuring, and optimizing modular data pipelines is newly required.
gaps.name: Data Pipeline Design and Automation
gaps.description: Ability to design, configure, and optimize automated, event-driven, modular data integration pipelines and manage their lifecycle.

gaps.justification: With growing reliance on metadata-rich, auditable workflows, a deeper understanding of data provenance, FAIR data principles, and metadata governance is required to enable discoverability, traceability, and interoperability.
gaps.name: Metadata Management and FAIR Principles
gaps.description: Expertise in curating, managing, and leveraging metadata in accordance with FAIR data principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) and supporting data lineage and provenance.

gaps.justification: Because platform integration and modular architecture are driven by microservices and interface contracts, the role now requires a solid understanding of service-oriented architecture, APIs, and data governance at the interface level.
gaps.name: Microservices and Integration Governance
gaps.description: Knowledge of microservice-based architectures, API management, interface governance, and the capabilities and limits of integration platform technologies.

gaps.justification: Automation shifts problem-solving from hands-on data wrangling to designing, abstracting, and governing integration logic and exception handling at scale.
gaps.name: Logic Abstraction and Rule Management
gaps.description: Ability to abstract integration logic, write formal data mapping/rule-sets, and manage exception handling in automated workflows.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities: 'Responsible for outreach and collaboration with a variety of stakeholders...in order to establish relationships to leverage new methods and data sources...and providing expert advice and analysis.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Stakeholder engagement must now include a focus on interoperable standards, platform reusability, and the establishment of data-sharing agreements that facilitate automated sourcing, rules-based linkage, and metadata exchange rather than one-off project arrangements.

gaps.justification: Collaboration shifts to include negotiation of data interface contracts, understanding of interoperability agreements, and collaborative governance of reusable integration rules.
gaps.name: Interface and Standards Negotiation
gaps.description: Skill in negotiating, adopting, and communicating standards and reusable contracts for automated data integration.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities: 'Implementation of various tools or software'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: The role will now implement, configure, and orchestrate automated integration and metadata management platforms and tools (rather than building custom scripts/tools for each data task).

gaps.justification: Adoption and optimal use of new toolsets require knowledge of emerging platforms for orchestrated, auditable automated integration (e.g., data integration platform-as-a-service, orchestration engines, etc.).
gaps.name: Platform Orchestration
gaps.description: Experience implementing and managing data integration and orchestration platforms, including workflow scheduling, monitoring, and exception alerting.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities: 'Ensuring overall quality and completeness of program results'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Quality assurance becomes an automated, metadata-driven process, with an emphasis on defining and monitoring rules, testing interface compatibility, and ensuring provenance rather than manual validation.

gaps.justification: Quality management pivots from transaction-based checking to automated rule-based monitoring, alerting, and exception management in complex pipelines.
gaps.name: Automated Quality and Exception Management
gaps.description: Skill in developing, testing, and managing automated quality control rules and exception workflows for integrated data pipelines.

update description: The future state of validation (GSBPM 5.3) shifts the entire error detection/validation workflow into automated, orchestrated processes. The Specialist’s role changes from hands-on validation and data manipulation to designing, overseeing, and evaluating the effectiveness of integrated, automated validation modules, orchestrating their interaction across subject-matter and data sources, and feeding back identified exceptions for rule improvement.
impact reasoning: The nature of data validation shifts from manual review to active design, monitoring, and iterative improvement of automated validation pipelines. This changes the Specialist's day-to-day work from execution to oversight, requiring interaction with technical teams and system architects, and making automation literacy as well as quality framework knowledge critical. Direct data manipulation is largely replaced by system-level oversight and exception management.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities: Manages activities related to: data integration, data manipulation, data analytics, processing, analysis and the preparation of dissemination and data visualization products. This involves setting objectives; leading program development, research or analysis; implementation of various tools or software, and ensuring overall quality and completeness of program results.
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: While the overall objective remains, the methods and focus shift heavily towards the design, management, and optimization of automated validation systems, rather than direct execution. Instead of hands-on validation, the Specialist will be accountable for specifying, evaluating, and refining validation rule logic with cross-functional teams.

gaps.justification: The shift to automated validation requires knowledge of how automated pipelines are constructed, monitored, and maintained.
gaps.name: Automated Validation Systems Design
gaps.description: Understanding of automated validation modules, workflow orchestration, and principles for building robust, maintainable, scalable validation rules across diverse data sources.

gaps.justification: The move toward system oversight over hands-on work requires the ability to diagnose, interpret, and feedback on exceptions raised by the automated system.
gaps.name: Exception Management and Feedback Loops
gaps.description: Ability to analyze validation exceptions flagged by automated systems, work with teams to refine rules, and implement process improvements based on exception evidence.

gaps.justification: Collaboration with pipeline designers and technical staff becomes central, requiring a new level of comfort with technical dialogue and solutioning.
gaps.name: Cross-Disciplinary Technical Communication
gaps.description: Skill in collaborating with data engineers, system architects, and subject-matter specialists to ensure validation workflows are correctly specified and fit-for-purpose.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities: Manages activities related to: ...ensuring overall quality and completeness of program results.
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: The Specialist will transition from quality assurance through manual intervention to oversight and continuous improvement of quality embedded in automated processes.

gaps.justification: Continuous process improvement in an automated validation context requires systematic thinking, knowledge of feedback mechanisms, and the ability to update or propose rule changes.
gaps.name: Continuous Quality Frameworks for Automated Validation
gaps.description: Ability to assess automated validation outputs, interpret quality metrics, and implement or recommend improvements within automated validation frameworks.

update description: Weighting is no longer handled through bespoke project routines, but through system-level, reusable, modular services that seamlessly process weights for integrated and alternative sources using standardized, AI-augmented methods as part of a pipeline.
impact reasoning: The specialist's current role, focused on hands-on weighting and bespoke data project routines, will shift towards designing, managing, and governing system-level modular weighting services. This necessitates a broader conceptualization of weighting logic, engagement with standardized and embedded AI methods, and involvement in governance and auditability of weighting pipelines. The role will further expand to include ongoing review of system and AI outputs, metadata management, and collaborative input to calibration and exception protocols.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - Bullet 1 ('Manages activities related to: data integration, data manipulation, data analytics, processing, analysis and the preparation of dissemination and data visualization products...')
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: The management of data integration and processing will shift away from direct data manipulation and bespoke routines to focus on designing and orchestrating modular, AI-augmented weighting pipelines. The specialist must ensure that weighting and integration processes are standardized, reusable, and auditable, with embedded logic that adapts to new data sources.

gaps.justification: Current specialist responsibilities emphasize hands-on, custom programming; transitioning to modular pipeline design and orchestration requires new skills in system architecture and workflow automation.
gaps.name: Modular Pipeline Design and Orchestration
gaps.description: Ability to architect, design, and oversee modular weighting pipelines that integrate diverse data sources and enable AI augmentation, ensuring standards compliance and reusability.

gaps.justification: Reviewing AI outputs and logs for weighting logic is new; specialists must understand AI model interpretability, anomaly detection within pipeline outputs, and how to adjust governance rules.
gaps.name: AI-Augmented Weighting Review and Auditability
gaps.description: Ability to critically review system-generated and AI-augmented weighting outputs, logs, and exceptions, identifying inaccuracies or adaptive issues and recommending refinements.

gaps.justification: Managing metadata and logic across weighting modules requires knowledge of data governance, metadata standards, and pipeline calibration protocols.
gaps.name: Metadata Governance and Weighting Logic Standardization
gaps.description: Comprehension of metadata standards, calibration procedures, and governance practices for modular weighting services within data pipelines.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - Bullet 3 ('Leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources to respond to user needs; develops mitigation strategies to address delays and briefs senior management when cost or scope changes are necessary.')
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Project leadership will now require specialists to coordinate the integration and management of modular, reusable services for weighting, focusing on system-level approaches rather than manual mitigation. Communication with senior management will extend to explaining system-wide changes, AI adaptive behaviors, and governance strategies.

gaps.justification: Specialists must shift from resolving project-level delays toward system-level monitoring and troubleshooting, addressing modular pipeline exceptions and calibration.
gaps.name: System-Level Troubleshooting and Calibration Governance
gaps.description: Ability to identify, communicate, and resolve issues arising in modular, AI-powered weighting pipelines, leveraging governance protocols and calibration frameworks.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities - (Implied)
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Technical activities will transition from bespoke programming and manual weighting to building, configuring, and testing modular weighting components that operate within orchestrated, AI-augmented pipelines.

gaps.justification: Modular components and AI-augmented logic require understanding of microservice architectures, pipeline orchestration platforms, and automated test protocols.
gaps.name: Microservices and Pipeline Orchestration
gaps.description: Ability to develop, configure, and oversee microservice architectures and orchestrated pipelines for reusable, automated data weighting and integration.

update description: Aggregation processes will transition from custom, programmatic, and manual implementations to standardized, automated microservices embedded within modular, centrally managed data pipelines. Specialists will be responsible for configuring, monitoring, and validating these modules, managing metadata lineage, and supporting exception handling and governance for audit and standardization.
impact reasoning: The work-description as currently formulated prioritizes hands-on, custom tool implementation and script development for core data processing activities. This update necessitates a shift from direct build-and-validate tasks toward orchestration of automated, reusable modules, requiring familiarity with both modern data pipeline tools and relevant governance processes. The Specialist will focus more on configuration, pipeline monitoring, validation, exception handling, and the maintenance of audit-ready metadata rather than heavy involvement in raw programming and ad hoc integration.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - Bullet 1: 'Manages activities related to: data integration, data manipulation, data analytics, processing, analysis and the preparation of dissemination and data visualization products. ... implementation of various tools or software ...'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: The focus shifts from manual or custom script-based tool implementation to configuring and validating centrally managed, automated aggregation modules within modular pipelines. The Key Activity should explicitly reference configuration, monitoring, validation, exception management, and metadata tracking activities in the automated data pipeline context.

gaps.justification: The transition to automated modular pipelines introduces requirements for managing pipeline configuration, metadata lineage, AI/microservice interpretability, and exception handling, which are not present in the current responsibilities.
gaps.name: Automated Data Pipeline Configuration and Orchestration
gaps.description: Understanding of configuring and monitoring modular, automated data pipeline components, including microservice orchestration platforms and workflow management systems.

gaps.justification: Tracking and maintaining metadata lineage for audit and reproducibility is new, as current work focuses mostly on programmatic implementation rather than metadata oversight.
gaps.name: Metadata Lineage and Auditability
gaps.description: Knowledge of metadata management tools and practices for ensuring data provenance, traceability, and supporting audit requirements.

gaps.justification: The use of AI-enabled aggregation microservices raises the need for interpretation and communication of such automated outputs, especially for exception management and transparency.
gaps.name: Interpretation of AI-enabled Data Aggregation Outputs
gaps.description: Ability to evaluate, explain, and document the logic and results generated by AI-based or automated aggregation modules, identifying potential exceptions or errors.

gaps.justification: Responsibility for supporting exception handling and contributing to processes that ensure governance and compliance is newly prominent due to the standardized/agile nature of modular workflows.
gaps.name: Exception Handling and Data Governance in Automated Workflows
gaps.description: Skill in developing, documenting, and enforcing exception-handling procedures within modular data workflows, and engaging in governance and standards compliance processes.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - Bullet 1: '... ensuring overall quality and completeness of program results.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Quality assurance responsibilities will now require leveraging built-in validation, monitoring, and audit mechanisms of the centralized aggregation modules, as well as proactively managing any exceptions in outputs.

gaps.justification: Existing QA practices focused on validating results of custom/handmade code; future work will require statistical and technical skills adapted to automated, modular validation mechanisms and AI explainability.
gaps.name: Validation and Quality Assessment in Automated Environments
gaps.description: Skill in leveraging automated monitoring, validation, and alerting systems for quality control in standardized data pipelines.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts (implied) - 'Implementation of various tools or software'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: This is de-emphasized in favor of configuration and orchestration of existing, standardized modules, reducing emphasis on custom tool development or scripting.

gaps.justification: Shift from development to orchestration means skills in modern pipeline configuration, rather than bespoke programming, become essential.
gaps.name: Configuration and Monitoring of Modular Data Pipelines
gaps.description: Skill in managing, configuring, and overseeing execution of automated aggregation modules in standardized environments (e.g., Airflow, Data Factory, etc.).

update description: Output drafting will be automated, shifting the role from technical assembly to overseeing system performance, ensuring quality of automated outputs, and handling exceptions, with new emphasis on interpretation and contextualization.
impact reasoning: As the responsibility for assembling and preparing draft outputs is transitioned to automated systems, the EC-06 Specialist's role will focus less on hands-on technical implementation (e.g., direct data manipulation and formatting for output). The new focus requires extensive oversight of automated systems and pipelines to ensure product quality and fit-for-purpose dissemination. The role also calls for interpreting and contextualizing automated outputs in response to user needs and to handle exceptions where automation might fail or produce ambiguous results.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - 'Manages activities related to: data integration, data manipulation, data analytics, processing, analysis and the preparation of dissemination and data visualization products. This involves setting objectives; leading program development, research or analysis; implementation of various tools or software, and ensuring overall quality and completeness of program results.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: This bullet will shift from describing technical involvement in output assembly and data visualization to a primary focus on managing, governing, and monitoring automated outputs, with significant attention to exception handling and validating analytical context of AI-generated results.

gaps.justification: The automation of drafting and assembling outputs means the specialist must develop greater expertise in automated pipeline monitoring, recognizing and troubleshooting failure points or inaccuracies.
gaps.name: Automated Data Pipeline Monitoring
gaps.description: Ability to monitor, diagnose, and maintain automated data output pipelines, responding effectively when errors or exceptions arise.

gaps.justification: Since outputs are no longer hands-on products, contextual review becomes critical to ensure AI-generated content aligns with analytical goals and user needs.
gaps.name: Analytical Interpretation and Contextualization of Automated Outputs
gaps.description: Capacity to evaluate and contextualize machine-produced outputs, checking for appropriateness, nuance, and correct interpretation in relation to the data's use case.

gaps.justification: Overseeing quality of automated outputs will require understanding both technical and analytical quality controls at a system level.
gaps.name: Quality Assurance in Automated Analytical Systems
gaps.description: Familiarity with practices to ensure accuracy, consistency, and completeness in AI-generated or automated analytic products.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - 'Authors analytical papers and other types of material supporting data development and dissemination.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Greater emphasis on interpreting and giving narrative/analytical context to automated outputs, rather than authoring based on direct manipulation/assembly.

gaps.justification: Shifting from direct authorship to interpreting AI-generated draft requires abilities in narrative validation and conceptual synthesis.
gaps.name: Output Interpretation and Narrative Synthesis
gaps.description: Skill in reviewing, validating, and translating automated data outputs into meaningful, user-oriented analytical products.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts (General)
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Shift from data assembly/visualization tool expertise to advanced systems monitoring, error diagnosis, and exception management.

gaps.justification: Role evolution from tool expert to AI/system overseer; requires troubleshooting, exception handling, and continual learning as automation evolves.
gaps.name: Automated System Troubleshooting and Exception Handling
gaps.description: Ability to detect, diagnose, and resolve issues in automated analytic data processing and output pipelines.

update description: Automation of data manipulation and standardized analysis shifts the EC-06 Specialist role from technical execution to more advanced interpretation, contextualization, and communication of insights. Routine technical tasks are automated; responsibilities now center on reviewing and assuring relevance, ethical soundness, and policy applicability of results produced by automated/AI-driven pipelines.
impact reasoning: The specialist’s everyday work will be less about running and managing technical data-processing activities, and more about interpreting results, ensuring their ethical and policy relevance, and communicating complex findings to broader audiences. The specialist will also serve as a reviewer and steward of automated outputs, addressing fairness, transparency, and responsible use, rather than setting objectives for data manipulation or performing technical integration work.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - Bullet 1: Manages activities related to: data integration, data manipulation, data analytics, processing, analysis and the preparation of dissemination and data visualization products...
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: The focus of this activity will be shifted away from direct management of data manipulation, processing, and analysis. Instead, it will entail overseeing, interpreting, and validating the automated work. The end product will now rest more on context-appropriate, ethical, and user-relevant interpretation.

gaps.justification: Identification of the new need to provide oversight and in-depth interpretation for automated analytics, which is not currently required.
gaps.name: Interpretation of Automated Analytical Outputs
gaps.description: Ability to critically review, contextualize, and interpret data products from automated/AI pipelines, understanding the limitations and strengths of automation.

gaps.justification: The evolving landscape shifts the primary output from technical accuracy to responsible and transparent communication, so practitioners need to learn how to communicate nuanced insights and the implications of automated findings effectively.
gaps.name: Communication of Automated Insights
gaps.description: Skill in translating complex, automated analytical results into accessible, policy-relevant, and ethically-grounded narratives for internal and external stakeholders.

gaps.justification: Oversight responsibilities for ethical and societal impacts now become central.
gaps.name: Ethical and Responsible AI Oversight
gaps.description: Understanding of AI/automation-related bias, fairness, transparency, and limitations applied to statistical and analytical workflows.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - Bullet 2: Responsible for outreach and collaboration with a variety of stakeholders...
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Stakeholder collaboration will increasingly involve ethical communication, contextual framing, and policy translation of results rather than negotiating data acquisition or technical issues.

gaps.justification: Interpreting and contextualizing automated outputs for diverse audiences requires new communication and framing abilities.
gaps.name: Stakeholder Communication on Automated Results
gaps.description: Ability to explain and discuss automated analysis processes, outputs, and ethical considerations with varied stakeholders, supporting trust and comprehension.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - Bullet 3: Leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources...
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Project leadership now must include managing, auditing, and validating automated pipelines for fairness, transparency, and alignment to organizational standards rather than directing manual data handling tasks.

gaps.justification: Project leadership in the new context involves oversight of automated systems, including periodic review for fairness, transparency, and fit-for-purpose.
gaps.name: Oversight of Automated Analytical Pipelines
gaps.description: Expertise in monitoring and assuring the quality, fairness, and transparency of automated and AI-based analytical solutions.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - Bullet 4: Authors analytical papers and other types of material supporting data development and dissemination.
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Analytical writing will now place greater emphasis on explaining how results were derived via automation/AI, ensuring transparency, and clarifying ethical and policy implications.

gaps.justification: Communicating automated methodology and ethical context is a new expectation.

gaps.description: Skill in documenting and disclosing the steps, assumptions, and limitations of automated data analytic methods in publications and communication material.
